encounter.notes: ARCHETYPE asset, not a single encounter. Skeletons are the largest measured creature archetype in the dungeon corpus - 62 distinct names, 822 appearances - and 100% of dungeon NPCs are capsules today. Catalogued as 'Boneman', which is why a sweep for 'skeleton' missed the whole family.

side_plates.why: The gallery publishes no full-body left or right profile; view-02 is a three-quarter and the rest are closeups. measure-view-coverage puts the cost at neither-camera 23.1% -> 18.3%, which is modest here because an upright A-pose humanoid is the shape two cameras cover best.

registration.verified_by: overlay reviewed 2026-09-08: one skull, one pair of glowing eye sockets, one tooth row, one cervical spine. No feature doubling anywhere. The base-plate skull is roughly 4% wider at the temples and its chin sits a few pixels lower, which reads as SOFT rather than doubled - the case the runbook explicitly prefers to a forced fit.

closeups.note: The FIRST closeup accepted on this project since the Saints, and it only registered because of --head-v-min. The automatic detector returns 0.7043 - the RIBCAGE - because a skeleton's widest upper row is the ribs, not the shoulders. At that band the match would have been ribs-to-ribs and the skull would never have been seen. Hand-set to 0.86, measured off the mesh (the skull occupies v 0.86-1.0 at x 0.40-0.60; the shoulders appear at v 0.82-0.86 spanning x 0.26-0.74).

closeups.rejected_reason: 13.23% at scale 0.265, against view-04's 11.44% on the same feature. It is a three-quarter skull, so it cannot register to a straight-on base plate as well as view-04 does; there is no reason to take the weaker of two plates for the same region.

4.84% - by far the lowest error measured on this subject, and rejected anyway. The ribcage, spine and pelvis align cleanly, but the overlay doubles both HANDS, offset outward and down by roughly a finger's length. Sixth confirmation on this project that width error is not a reliability signal. The base plate already covers the torso squarely, so there is nothing to gain against a real risk of smeared hands.

reference.closeup_note: One accepted (the skull), two rejected. Accepting a closeup at all is unusual here - 15 consecutive candidates were rejected across the three assets built earlier in this session - and it was only possible because the head band could be hand-set.

geometry.provenance: Tencent Hunyuan3D-2mv (fp16, 50 steps, octree 380, seed 12345) from the letterboxed view-01/view-03 plates (1052px square). Draft: 287,774 faces, 84.1s. The concern going in was that a skeleton is mostly holes - thin bones and gaps that two-view reconstruction would fuse into a mannequin. It did not: the clay render resolves individual ribs, the pelvis, a segmented spine, separated fore/upper arm bones and articulated hands. Screened at 23.1% blind BEFORE any projection time, comfortably inside the shipped band of 5.6-31.5%.
geometry.budget_note: Lesser-enemy budget: ~5,000 triangles and a 512px atlas, because skeletons appear dozens at a time.

regions.note: HAND-SET, not the detector's value. The detector returns 0.7043 because a skeleton's widest upper-body row is the RIBCAGE, not the shoulders - a failure mode not previously recorded (the known ones are head ornaments, robe cones and wingspans). Measured on the mesh: skull v 0.86-1.0 spanning x 0.40-0.60; shoulders v 0.82-0.86 spanning x 0.26-0.74.
